sections.content: How many people stayed in Doncaster after gaining qualifications?

Doncaster is a large town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Doncaster does not have its own university.

Doncaster has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Doncaster ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 5,215 state-school pupils from Doncaster who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,480 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,430 (27%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Doncaster to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Doncaster's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Doncaster in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Doncaster move to?

Of Doncaster's graduates, 560 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 115 of those graduates (21%) were living fairly locally, in the Doncaster travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Doncaster's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 420 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 210 of those qualified non-graduates (50%) were living fairly locally, in the Doncaster travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Doncaster's GCSE cohort:

  • 325 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 125 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 24% of graduates and 29% of qualified non-graduates living in Doncaster had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,165 graduates and 1,385 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Doncaster. This is compared with the 1,480 graduates and 1,430 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 76% of the graduates had also lived in Doncaster as GCSE pupils, while 24% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Doncaster in 2018 to 2019, 71% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
